name: Namada Shielded Pools
rootCause: On June 19, 2026, approximately $600,000 in assets (ATOM, USDC, OSMO, TIA, NYM, etc.) were drained from Namada’s Multi-Asset Shielded Pool (MASP) through an IBC Transfer Logic Exploit. The loss initially went unnoticed because a stale indexer continued displaying funds as available, while live RPC queries showed zero balances on the chain. The attacker swept shielded IBC assets cross-chain. Namada confirmed the exploit and is investigating.

descriptions.text: On June 19, 2026, approximately $600,000 in assets (ATOM, USDC, OSMO, TIA, NYM, etc.) were drained from Namada’s Multi-Asset Shielded Pool (MASP) through an IBC Transfer Logic Exploit. The loss initially went unnoticed because a stale indexer continued displaying funds as available, while live RPC queries showed zero balances on the chain. The attacker swept shielded IBC assets cross-chain. Namada confirmed the exploit and is investigating.

On June 19, 2026, Namada's Multi-Asset Shielded Pool (MASP) was drained via an IBC transfer logic flaw. Approximately $600,000 in assets,including ATOM, USDC, OSMO, TIA, and NYM,were swept from the privacy pool. The loss was masked at first due to a stale indexer, leaving balances falsely visible. A flaw in Namada's implementation of IBC transfer logic enabled unauthorized withdrawals from the shielded pool, allowing an attacker to drain assets without proper accounting or verification. The privacy-by-design features and lagging indexer delayed detection.
